title: Human-Water Systems
objective: Model human-system pressures and governance responses shaping groundwater outcomes.
questions: How do abstraction and infrastructure systems modify subsurface quantity and quality trajectories?
Which policy interventions reduce potable-water risk across scenarios?

specialSections.title: Abstraction
specialSections.body: Characterize withdrawal intensity, distribution, and timing across sectors.

specialSections.title: Demand
specialSections.body: Represent domestic, agricultural, and industrial demand trajectories under uncertainty.

specialSections.title: Sewer and Pipeline Leakage
specialSections.body: Capture leakage pathways that alter recharge and contamination conditions.

specialSections.title: Mining and Industry
specialSections.body: Model extraction and industrial activity impacts on groundwater quantity and quality.

specialSections.title: Irrigation Return Flow
specialSections.body: Estimate delayed return-flow contributions and pollutant transport effects.

specialSections.title: Engineered Recharge
specialSections.body: Assess managed aquifer recharge interventions for resilience and recovery.

specialSections.title: Feedback Mechanisms
specialSections.body: Model two-way socio-hydrological feedbacks between behavior, infrastructure, and aquifer response.

specialSections.title: Governance Scenarios
specialSections.body: Translate regulation and policy levers into scenario constraints and outcomes.

tasks.title: Demand and Abstraction Modelling
tasks.summary: Characterize domestic, agricultural, and industrial groundwater demand and pumping behavior.

tasks.title: Infrastructure and Governance Coupling
tasks.summary: Represent leakage, sanitation, and policy drivers as model forcing terms.

tasks.title: Scenario Delivery
tasks.summary: Deliver intervention and future-development scenarios for WP3, WP4, and WP6.
